THE LORD SPEAKS · ISAIAH 43:19

The Word · KJV

ISAIAH 43:18–19 · KING JAMES VERSION

18 Remember ye not the former things, neither consider the things of old.

19 Behold, I will do a new thing; now it shall spring forth; shall ye not know it? I will even make a way in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert.

Four Movements of the Promise

01 / RELEASE

Former Things

“Remember ye not the former things” — the command redirects attention from what has been toward what God announces.

02 / BEHOLD

A New Thing

“Now it shall spring forth” — God's declaration calls for recognition, not merely anticipation.

03 / DIRECTION

A Way

“A way in the wilderness” — a path where the landscape appears to offer none.

04 / PROVISION

Rivers

“Rivers in the desert” — life-giving provision in a place associated with scarcity.

From Wilderness to Water

THE SETTING

Remember the speaker

In Isaiah 43, the LORD addresses His people and speaks of redemption and deliverance. This promise belongs first to that prophetic context.

THE TURN

Behold the new

The passage contrasts former mighty acts with a new work God declares He will do. The call is to perceive His action.

THE RESPONSE

Walk with hope

As a devotional application, ask where old expectations may obscure attention to God's guidance, without assuming every personal plan is a divine promise.

Reflection & Prayer

SELECT A REFLECTION

What past event, expectation, or disappointment occupies so much attention that it becomes difficult to notice what is before you?

Prayer: LORD, teach me to hear Your Word faithfully, remember Your works rightly, and trust Your wisdom for the road ahead. Amen.
